companies.name: Moldex-Metric (Moldex-Metric, Inc.; Moldex/Metric AG & Co. KG)
companies.fit_notes: RECOMMENDED. Strongest fit found. Hearing and respiratory protection is its stated expertise (mdx-core), though it also lists eye protection and hearing's share of sales is unknown. It makes the products itself with a stated high level of vertical integration (mdx-vert, mdx-foam). Size is mid-sized, not a giant, although current global headcount is not public: 350+ in Europe (mdx-eu) and 450 in Los Angeles in 2020 (mdx-private). Every channel I could find is distributors and industrial supply (mdx-channel), and no sleep, music, travel or other consumer line appeared on either the US or European site, so the consumer question looks open. That is absence of evidence, not proof. The most useful angle: foam and moulding know-how came from a bra-cup business (mdx-origin), which suggests a firm that has moved materials know-how between markets before. That reading is my inference. Evidence opened: full US catalogue PDF, hearing technical briefs index, patent information page, hearing FAQ, German legal notice. Contradictions: the US homepage gives two different patent counts (mdx-patents), and 'family-owned' could not be confirmed.
unknown: Revenue, profit and hearing protection's share of sales. No public accounts were opened for either entity.
Current ownership. Founder-led and privately held in 2020, but the Metric Products link is sourced only to a 2005 article, and 'family-owned' is not confirmed.

How the US entity and the European entity relate. The legal notice names Moldex/Metric AG (Zurich) and Moldex Inc. (Nevada) as partners, and European managing directors with a different surname from the US founder. Control is not clear.
Whether the German KG's accounts are on the Unternehmensregister. Not checked.

Whether individuals buy meaningful volume. Search snippets showed bulk packs on Galaxus, eBay and marketplaces, but the Galaxus page returned HTTP 403 and was not opened. No consumer-format pack was confirmed.
Customer lists, unit volumes and distributor terms: not public.

companies.name: Cotral Lab
companies.fit_notes: RECOMMENDED. Most focused hearing-protection specialist found, with the sharpest strategic question, although it now also sells prescription safety eyewear and, through Comu Systems, tactical communications (ctl-deal). It makes custom-moulded protectors itself (ctl-3d) with in-house filters (ctl-filter) and has a Bluetooth product (ctl-it1). Its model looks built for companies, not individuals: technicians take impressions on site (ctl-onsite) and sales go mainly direct to employers (ctl-channel). A consumer move would have to replace that fitting model, and I found no consumer product on the French or English sites. It is also newly owned by a PPE distributor (ctl-deal), so a consumer move would also be an ownership-level question. Both readings are my inference. Evidence opened: company sites (FR and EN), technical blog, legal notice, regional agency profile, dated French business press. Contradictions: size varies by source and date (ctl-size25, ctl-size26), and the English site still shows the founder as Chairman and CEO while the French site names two general managers (ctl-lead). A search summary attributed a music, aviation, swimming and sleep range to Cotral; on opening the directory page, that row belongs to Quies, so it was discarded.
unknown: Filed accounts. Revenue is reported as both EUR 50m and EUR 60m and was not checked against a registry filing (RCS Caen 402 960 637).
Current headcount: 350 and 380 are both reported.
Price paid for Cotral Lab: not disclosed in anything opened.
Why Cotral needed 'structural support'. The phrase is on record but no detail was found.
Whether Cotral has any individual-buyer route, such as through audiologists. None found, but not disproved.

companies.name: Hellberg Safety (Hultafors Group, owned by Investment AB Latour)
companies.fit_notes: RECOMMENDED, with one caveat. Small hearing and face protection specialist inside a larger group, and the only finalist whose parent publishes regular financial reports (hlb-owner, hlb-sales). It already has consumer footholds that make the question concrete: a children's earmuff (hlb-junior) sold by general retailers (hlb-bauhaus, hlb-kjell) and a retailer locator (hlb-retail). But that is one product and not a consumer strategy, and the group states its focus as professionals (hlb-pro) while Hellberg's stated ambition is head protection (hlb-head). So a real tension exists between the Junior foothold and the professional strategy. It has the electronics capability a lifestyle product might use (hlb-tech). Evidence opened: Latour press release and year-end report, Junior product page with attenuation data, catalogue page, retailer listings. Declaration of Conformity link seen but not opened. Caveat: the only Hellberg-specific financials are 2017, because it has since been reported inside Hultafors Group, and head protection now appears to matter as much as hearing.
unknown: Hellberg's current revenue and headcount. The SEK 66m and about 20 staff figures are for 2017, and nothing later was found.
Whether production is still in-house at Stenkullen. The 2018 statement could not be confirmed as current.
Share of sales through consumer retail, and Junior's volumes: not public.
Hearing versus head protection share of Hellberg's sales.
Latour's full 2025 annual report was not opened, only the year-end report.
Which attenuation figure is right for Junior: Hellberg says up to 25 dB(A), while a search snippet for Kjell said 24 dB. The Kjell figure was not confirmed.
